value.body: Packaging technologists decide how a product is packed so it stays safe, lasts on the shelf and can be made and shipped efficiently. Food, beverage, pharma and consumer goods companies and packaging converters hire them. Work moves between the lab, vendor meetings and trials on production lines.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech Food Technology, packaging or chemical engineering

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Material testing equipment, shelf-life studies, specification sheets

items.label: Packaging industry size
items.source: Industry estimates cited by IMAP (as reported)

items.label: Projected size
items.note: A projection, not a measured figure
items.source: Avendus Capital report via IBEF (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join packaging development or quality teams in food and consumer goods companies, or packaging manufacturers. A postgraduate diploma in packaging is a common add-on for those who want to specialise.

value.title: At a glance
items: Plastic-waste and recycling rules are reshaping material choices.
Next steps: packaging manager, sustainability or R&D roles.
Plant-based roles may involve shifts during line trials.
